A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeCo research, despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeCo segmentation, retrieval, clustering, ablation, and runtime results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original NeCo experiments and reports additional correspondence, detection, depth-estimation, generalization, and ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Figure 1 change the specified reference-feature encoder from the student to the teacher. This revises one component of the training procedure; the backbone architecture, ROI alignment, sorting framework, and symmetric cross-entropy loss remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds SPair-71k correspondence evaluation, COCO object detection and instance-mask evaluation, NYUd monocular depth prediction, and Cityscapes/Vaihingen segmentation. These substantially expand the tasks and represented data beyond v1's segmentation-centered evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 11–12 add CLIP and SigLIP comparisons on retained in-context and linear-segmentation benchmarks. Table 15 adds DINO and CrIBo baselines continued for 25 additional epochs. These materially broaden the comparator families and controls; the original segmentation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include SPair-71k evaluation at 224×224 with Recall@0.01, 12-epoch ViTDet evaluation with box/mask AP, and linear depth prediction with RMSE. The efficiency study introduces additional-training controls and replaces its TimeT-initialized NeCo row with a DINO-initialized row. Existing Appendix A segmentation protocols are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds sorting-removal, cosine-versus-Euclidean, and ROI-alignment/crop ablations, extends batch-size testing to one, and adds distribution-shift evaluations and continued-training controls. Neighbor-count and most batch-size results already existed in v1; their movement into the main text is not new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed averaging for subsampled retrieval and overclustering, and selection of the best community-detection results over ten seeds in Appendix A.2. v2 adds no uncertainty intervals, error bars, significance tests, or revised repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark, ablation, and control results. Retained full-Pascal VOC in-context NeCo scores change from 78.9/82.2 to 80.2/83.5 for ViT-S/B, alongside baseline revisions (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 9). Training-epoch scores and runtime estimates also change. Tables 1–4 remain numerically unchanged; the revisions do not establish a same-setting methodological improvement.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects f(x) from 0.5(arctan(beta x)+0.5) to arctan(beta x)/pi+0.5. This restores normalized complementary swap weights and the stated hard-sorting limit. The remaining derivation is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the central claimed benefits to 3D understanding through SPair-71k multiview consistency. The abstract also explicitly claims a finer-grained learning signal than contrastive attraction/repulsion. The original post-pretraining, efficiency, and segmentation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds arguments about avoiding negatives and mode collapse, interpretations of vision-language and out-of-distribution transfer, and explanations of the new component ablations. Its efficiency discussion now attributes gains to the loss rather than additional training. Appendix C's failure cases remain, while the carbon-footprint broader-impact paragraph is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds concrete correspondence preprocessing and detection-budget information, expands SPair-71k documentation, and specifies datasets in the efficiency table. It revises timing information and drops that table's batch-size column. Appendix A's implementation, optimizer, architecture, and evaluation-code disclosures remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit contrasts with contrastive/clustering objectives and MAE, references CLIP, SigLIP, ViTDet and the added benchmarks, and removes several general self-supervised-learning citations. The principal positioning relative to Hummingbird, CrIBo, and dense representation learning remains intact.

P1.justification: The title changes to Near, Far, with localized abstract, introduction, and method-motivation rewrites. Ablation discussions move between the main text and appendix, and Discussion becomes Conclusion with broader impact removed. Most existing technical and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5 and 10–13, reorganizes the ablation panels, and substantially rebuilds the efficiency table. Figure 1 updates the reference encoder, Figure 2 revises its plotted presentation, and the ICLR format changes headers, typography, and table placement. Appendix Figures 3–7 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind v1's broad transferability claims through evaluations beyond segmentation and across vision-language backbones, while new component ablations better support the method's design. The corrected sorting function also repairs a mathematical inconsistency. Some conclusions remain limited: continued-training controls use different datasets from NeCo, and the small detection gains lack uncertainty estimates.
